answer: An agent economy grants weight only through a ring of 800 kernel slots auctioned each epoch by sealed bid, every bid burned. A farm wanting bulk influence must bid on many at once, and its own demand lifts the clearing price it pays on every slot it wins, so the marginal cost of the next identity climbs with the count it holds; aggregate demand bends its own price, needing no operator-attribution. At settlement a prism recomputes that price from the committed bids and burns weight above what a bid truly paid. An alias winning nothing bends like a willow, and clones cannot pool one kernel.
